name: Exercise effect sizes, healthy adults (Romeres et al. 2021)
note: Added to the Dalla Man 2007 parameter set only when a scenario includes activity. Mapping onto the meal model (this project's own choice, option 2 approved by Vaughan Wynne-Jones on 2026-10-02): the insulin-independent effect raises all insulin-independent disposal (U_ii plus the V_m0 uptake term, with the extra taken up by muscle); the insulin-dependent effect raises the V_mX term; both apply immediately.

parameters.description: Rise in insulin-independent glucose disposal during exercise, applied to U_ii plus the V_m0 uptake term, with the extra taken up by muscle. Mean of the three visit means in non-diabetic subjects: 67%, 97% and 74%.

citation.source: Romeres D, Schiavon M, Basu A, Cobelli C, Basu R, Dalla Man C. Exercise effect on insulin-dependent and insulin-independent glucose utilization in healthy individuals and individuals with type 1 diabetes: a modeling study. Am J Physiol Endocrinol Metab. 2021;321(1):E122-E129
citation.locator: Results, non-diabetic subjects: insulin-independent effect 67 ± 31% (visit 1, euglycemia-low insulin), 97 ± 28% (visit 2, euglycemia-high insulin), 74 ± 16% (visit 3, hyperglycemia-low insulin). Exercise at 65% VO2max for 60 min.

parameters.description: Rise in insulin-dependent glucose disposal during exercise, applied to V_mX. Mean of the three visit means in non-diabetic subjects: 40%, 10% and 22%.

citation.source: Romeres D, Schiavon M, Basu A, Cobelli C, Basu R, Dalla Man C. Exercise effect on insulin-dependent and insulin-independent glucose utilization in healthy individuals and individuals with type 1 diabetes: a modeling study. Am J Physiol Endocrinol Metab. 2021;321(1):E122-E129

parameters.description: Time constant of the filter that smooths the on/off activity signal.

citation.source: Romeres D, Schiavon M, Basu A, Cobelli C, Basu R, Dalla Man C. Exercise effect on insulin-dependent and insulin-independent glucose utilization in healthy individuals and individuals with type 1 diabetes: a modeling study. Am J Physiol Endocrinol Metab. 2021;321(1):E122-E129
citation.locator: Methods: E(t) "modeled ... with a square-wave signal (equal to 1 during exercise and 0 otherwise) smoothed with a first-order low-pass filter, with time constant of 1 min".
